 At Jammu

sentences.text: The petitioner is one of three accused persons who have been put up for trial borne out of investigation of FIR No. 19/2024 registered for alleged commission of offences under sections 409/420/467/468/471/477-A/120-B Indian Penal Code (IPC), 1860 registered by the Police Station, Arnas.

2. The registration of the said FIR had taken place with the Police Station Arnas but later on investigation came to be shifted to Police Station, Crime Branch, Jammu which came up with the production of a police report (preliminary challan) No. Nil before the court of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Reasi against three accused persons, namely, Ajeet Kumar, Ali Hussain Shah and the petitioner herein-Balbir Singh.
The sequence of the three accused persons in the challan is that accused No. 1 is Ali Hussain Shah, the petitioner herein Balbir Singh as accused No. 2 and Ajeet Kumar as accused No. 3.

sentences.text: The subject matter of the investigation is related to alleged acts of omission and commission amounting to defalcation on the part of the three accused persons in conduct of two major heads i.e., Pensions 2071 and NPS 8342 for a period w.e.f., 04.05.2023 to 01.03.2024.

Thus, the three accused persons have been found by the investigating authority to be involved in Criminal Breach of Trust and Misappropriation of Govt. Funds (409 IPC), Forgery for the purpose of cheating (467, 468 IPC), Falsification of accounts (477-A IPC), Criminal Conspiracy (120-B IPC) and use of forged documents as genuine (471 IPC).
4.
The petitioner came to be arrested in this case on 14.03.2024 and ever since then he is in the custody as being an undertrial.

5. One of the three accused persons, namely, Ajeet Kumar came to approach this Court, after having suffered rejection of his bail from the trial court, with a bail application No. 151/2024 which came to be disposed of on merits by this Court by virtue of a judgment dated 25.11.2024 thereby granting bail in his favour.

6. The presentation of the preliminary chargesheet against the three accused persons by the Police Station, Crime Branch, Jammu took place on 12.06.2024.
7.

The petitioner, at the first instance, had also come to this Court with bail petition No. 155/2024 which came to be allowed to be withdrawn by him with liberty to approach the trial court in view of the development during the pendency of his said bail petition that the preliminary chargesheet had come to be submitted by the Police Station, Crime Branch Jammu before the Court of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Reasi and accordingly this Court, in terms of an order dated 18.09.2024,
allowed the withdrawal of said bail petition by the petitioner with liberty to approach the trial court for seeking bail.
8.

The petitioner having preferred fresh bail application before the trial court of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Reasi has come to suffer rejection of the bail application in terms of an order dated 02.12.2024 the undertone of which is that since offence under section 409 Indian Penal Code (IPC), 1860 carries life imprisonment as maximum punishment having a bar attached to seeking of bail in such like case in terms of section 480 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS),
2023 and the investigation of the case is still incomplete and the charges in the preliminary chargesheet are yet to be framed
as such no ground is made out for grant of bail in favour of the petitioner.

9. A perusal of the order dated 02.12.2024 would show that the trial court is not cognizant of the fact that one of the three accused persons, namely, Ajeet Kumar has already earned bail during the very pendency of the preliminary chargesheet before the court of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Reasi.

It is in this backdrop that the petitioner has come forward with this petition under section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 corresponding to section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
10. Prima facie case is made out.

sentences.text: 11. Issue notice to the respondent.
12. Mrs. Monika Kohli, learned Sr. AAG accepts notice on behalf of the respondent.
She seeks and is allowed two weeks time to file reply.
13. Through the medium of the instant application-CrlM No. 1929/2024, the petitioner is seeking indulgence of this Court for grant of interim bail in his favour.

14. Considering the fact that one of the three accused persons, namely, Ajeet Kumar has also been admitted to regular bail during the very pendency of the preliminary chargesheet and further that the trial court is awaiting for the filing of a supplementary chargesheet without any time line given for doing the same, the petitioner cannot be made to suffer the custody as an incarceration and,
therefore, this Court finds that case is made out for grant of interim bail at this stage of the case.
15.

Accordingly, interim bail is granted in favour of the petitioner subject to furnishing of bail bond before the Superintendent District Jail, Udhampur of an amount of Rs. 1,00,000/- (rupees one lac)
and surety bond of the like amount to the satisfaction of the Registrar Judicial, Jammu.

The petitioner to ensure his regular attendance on each and every date of hearing before the court of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Reasi without any miss except on health grounds and further the petitioner not to indulge in any act of omission and commission in any manner whatsoever aiming to influence or intervene in the course of investigation or trial of the case.
This direction to operate till next of hearing.
16. List again on 31.12.2024.

(RAHUL BHARTI) JUDGE JAMMU 11.12.2024 Naresh/Secy.
